clue.text: It is cut at union meeting

definitions.text: It is cut at union meeting

parts.words: It is cut at union meeting
parts.note: a union meeting reads as a trade-union gathering, but here it is a marriage ceremony, at whose reception a tiered confection is ceremonially sliced

explanation.surface: Something gets cut back at a trade union meeting, perhaps funding or jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' sounds industrial; it means a marriage, and the thing cut is the centrepiece of the reception.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding reception the couple traditionally slice the iced, tiered confection together.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words basket chair, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Someone takes their meal outdoors sitting in a wicker chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' suggests dining out; here it means corrode, as acid does to a metal plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to corrode a surface with acid, literally eating it away.

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
rum is an old British slang word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A dead, odd kettle sitting unused in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kettle' is a kitchen kettle in the surface but is the kettledrum, the orchestra's timpani; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettledrum is one example of a percussion instrument of this kind.

definitions.meaning: the fourth book of the Old Testament
read as '...', things that make you numb, a whimsical coinage

explanation.definitionFit: It is a Bible book, and jokingly also means agents that numb, since anaesthetics deaden sensation.

definitions.meaning: the actors in a play collectively
to pitch or toss is to throw, as one throws a line or a die

explanation.definitionFit: The actors in a production are its company, and to throw something is to fling or hurl it.

clue.text: King ordering Merlin in the citadel

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

indicators.note: ordering means putting the letters of Merlin into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: King Arthur commanding his wizard Merlin within the castle stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures Arthur commanding his wizard; 'ordering' is the anagram signal, not a royal command, and 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moscow Kremlin is a fortified citadel at the heart of the city.

parts.note: a person always puffing on Virginia tobacco cigarettes, lighting each from the last as if linked together

explanation.surface: Someone forever busy and breathless in the US state of Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia is a type of tobacco, not the state; 'constantly-engaged' hints at links in a continuous series.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lights one cigarette from the previous one smokes without a break.

clue.text: Sligo potter gone bust he is probably on the rocks

definitions.text: he is probably on the rocks

indicators.note: something gone bust is broken up, so the letters of the two words are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A potter from Sligo whose business has failed is probably in financial trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' means ruined in the surface; literally the scientist works on rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies the origin and composition of rocks is literally on them.

clue.text: Eg brogue often lost at Ascot

definitions.meaning: a brogue is a type of stout leather footwear
racehorses at Ascot racecourse frequently cast a metal plate from a hoof

explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is footwear, and a racehorse's hoof carries an iron plate that can come off in a race.

clue.text: Maestro cuts out leader of boys' band

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conductor slashes part of a boy band leader's music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boys' band' suggests a pop group; it is a troop of Scouts.
explanation.definitionFit: The adult in charge of a troop of Scouts holds this title.

definitions.meaning: a row or level in a hierarchy
one layer of the wedding confection at 1 across

explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or row in a ranking, and also one stacked layer of a celebratory cake.

clue.text: Remus, for one, has soup in bad winter

indicators.note: in means the soup goes inside the rearranged letters
bad signals the letters of winter going wrong, rearranged

parts.note: broth is a thin soup

explanation.surface: Someone named Remus is eating soup during a harsh winter.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus and Romulus were the legendary founders of Rome, born together; 'bad' signals the anagram and 'in' the container, while 'has' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Remus was the sibling born with Romulus, the founding pair of Rome.

indicators.note: can be implies the letters of Leeds habits could be made into another word by rearranging

explanation.surface: Habits in the city of Leeds can be resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' is the anagram signal: LEEDS HABITS can be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something established is fixed and settled in place.

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: We retract what was said about a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' only links WE to the next piece, and 'back' is not a reversal but a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy film set in the American frontier is a genre of movie.

indicators.note: inside means the R goes within the word for snowfield

parts.note: névé is granular snow at the head of a glacier, a snowfield

explanation.surface: Bravery is needed out on a snowfield.
explanation.walkthrough: NEVE is the crossword-familiar word for a glacier snowfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is boldness or courage in a daunting situation.

clue.text: Which fire-opal makes a girl so excited?

indicators.note: excited suggests agitated, so the letters of a girl so are stirred up

explanation.surface: A fiery gem that thrills a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which' and 'makes' are link words around the anagram of A GIRL SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Girasol is the name for a fire-opal, a gem showing reddish light.

clue.text: Saints in camp, full of idle talk

indicators.note: in means the saints go within the word for camp

parts.note: camp is old slang for gay

explanation.surface: Saints at a camp chattering endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' is a noun in the surface but means flamboyant here.
explanation.definitionFit: Gassy is informal for talkative, full of empty chatter.

indicators.note: macabre here signals the letters of the word danse have been gruesomely mangled

explanation.surface: Saint-Saëns's piece Danse Macabre playing in an American bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon' looks like a bar; it is the US term for a saloon car, the British name for a sedan. 'Danse Macabre' is a familiar title, which hides the split.
explanation.definitionFit: The British saloon car is called a sedan in American usage.

clue.text: First chap to use arc-lighting, they say

definitions.text: First chap to use arc-lighting, they say

parts.words: First chap to use arc-lighting, they say
parts.note: arc sounds like ark, so the first man to use an ark: the Biblical patriarch of the Flood

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be the pioneer of electric arc lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arc' is said like 'ark', and 'they say' signals the sound; the builder of the Ark is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch builds the Ark to survive the Flood.

parts.note: a son is a boy child

indicators.note: the opening of glee-club is its first letter

explanation.surface: A boy's debut at the glee club is a cause for celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'opening' takes the first letter of glee-club.
explanation.definitionFit: A song can be a hymn or paean sung in celebration.

clue.text: Stop at sea has a huge following

indicators.note: following means the word for huge comes after the a

parts.note: vast means huge

explanation.surface: A naval stoppage draws a large crowd of followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a noun for supporters; it says VAST comes after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a sailor's command meaning stop or hold.

parts.note: pitch read not as slope but as the black tarry material spread over a flat roof

explanation.surface: Asking about the angle of a roof's slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests roof angle; it is the bituminous material. The OCR 'ofthe' is 'of the'.
explanation.definitionFit: This bitumen mixture is used for roofing and paving, a type of tarry material.

clue.text: Cut of beef for the league leaders

definitions.meaning: a lean joint from the upper leg of beef
the team at the head of a league table

explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean joint of beef, and as two words the leading team in a league table.

definitions.meaning: to sink back, as a patient slipping into illness again
to decline after improving, falling back

explanation.surface: Something about to get worse and collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to sink back into illness after recovery, worsening again.

clue.text: From Orkneys to city in New York State

indicators.note: from ... to signals changing the word Orkneys into something new, a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Travelling from the Scottish Orkney islands to a New York city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' and 'to' read as a journey but mark the change of ORKNEYS into a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonkers is a city in Westchester County bordering the Bronx.

definitions.meaning: a chalk stream in Hampshire, England, famous for fly-fishing
a trial is an experiment or examination

explanation.definitionFit: The Test is a Hampshire river, and a trial is an examination.

indicators.note: endless means the word for danger loses its final letter

parts.note: peril means danger

explanation.surface: A fairy in never-ending danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the L from PERIL. A peri is a fairy in Persian myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a sprite of Persian mythology, a winged spirit.

indicators.note: among means the word for dry goes between the ducks

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks are two O's
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A monarch staying dry amid ducks on the pond.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, hence O. Otto was the name of several German and Holy Roman emperors and kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto I was crowned king of Germany before becoming emperor.
Feeling down means feeling low, and Down is a county in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Cursing is men's way of speaking

parts.note: male means belonging to men
diction is one's manner of enunciation

explanation.surface: Swearing is how men talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A malediction is a curse, the uttering of evil wishes.

parts.note: read as compass points, east then west then east then south, a zigzag course ending at south

explanation.surface: Creatures weaving their way southwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are compass points, E, W, E, S, tracing a zigzag that finishes heading south; the animals are female sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Female sheep are farm animals.

clue.text: Why is factory not producing? Pound tied up!

parts.note: to pound is to hit or strike
bound means tied up

explanation.surface: A frustrated owner wonders why the factory is idle, with money stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' suggests money; it is a verb meaning hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory immobilised by industrial action is halted by workers' walkout.
